routes.reason: A0-extension plans relative Pic⁰ representability, not the numerical Picard local system of an arbitrary proper scheme, Brauer obstructions or descent of contractions; this Part II extends AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry in that direction and its title has the parent prefix. The review added nine missing items (Picard scheme and τ-part, torsor torsion, the Brauer obstruction, semiample contractions and their descent, the Brauer group of a finite algebra, surface contractions, negativity of exceptional curves, Zariski connectedness) and item 186 (openness of ampleness for algebraic spaces, not named by R09.1).

Néron-model layers R11.2/R11.4 do not classify genus-one fibrations or rational elliptic surfaces over F₂; the Part II is justified. The review corrected its brief: Theorem 10.4 has eleven nonzero-j models, not eight (three found by exhaustive search), and the classification should be planned as a finite computation using the criterion #J(F₂) = 25. It added the three models and eight further missing items (genus-one fibrations, Zariski's lemma, conductor squares, ordinary/supersingular curves, normalisation under base change, geometrically rational surfaces, Shioda–Tate, the Picard group of the generic fibre).
R25.3 is the abelian-variety obstruction; Fontaine's Hodge-vanishing theorem for K3 surfaces is a genuinely new endpoint in that direction.
The rank-two Oort–Tate classification is a concrete source for R07.1.

The algebraic-cycle point-count formulas are worked realisations of WC.7; the review added the Tate-twisted Frobenius convention and the point-count criterion for constant Picard of a rational surface.

No layer plans Enriques surfaces or their nonexistence over Z; a new roadmap is justified. The review found that the main theorem's printed proof has a gap: Proposition 11.1's table and §§11–15 omit three Jacobian configurations (from the incomplete Theorem 10.4). The brief now says the roadmap must exclude them, records that the extraction's repair of Proposition 5.5 (items 173–188) is sound, and lists five further missing items.
The triviality of π₁(Spec Z) is a concrete Galois-category application of IG.0.
Rigidification and representation of Picard classes with a section supply A0-extension; the review added the low-degree Leray sequence for G_m.
Henselian section lifting belongs to SF.1/SF.2; the review added descent of properness and global sections along field extensions.

notes: Independent review by Claude Code, session cc-39fac3, 23 September 2026, of the extraction by cc-442dc5 (with earlier Codex runs). The published version (Ann. of Math. 197 (2023), 1–63) is paywalled, so the review read arXiv v3 (identical after the first page to the author's version of 19 July 2022, which the extraction read) and its TeX source in full again, with four checkers splitting the paper; the coordinator verified the main finding independently. Main finding: Theorem 10.4's list of rational elliptic surfaces over F₂ with non-zero functional j is incomplete. An exhaustive search over all 2²¹ Weierstrass equations with Tate's algorithm gives three further models (I₂*+E₄+Ĩ₂, I₃*+E₄+Ĩ₁, IV*+E₄+Ĩ₂), and the coordinator's independent point counts (Σ_t #J_t(F_q) = 1 + 10q + q² for q = 2, 4, 8, 16) confirm constant Picard scheme. Proposition 11.1 and §§11–15 omit these configurations, so the printed proof of Theorem 15.1, and hence of the main Theorem 5.1, has a gap at that step; whether they occur on a non-exceptional Enriques surface over F₂ is not settled here. Other changes: 26 statements and 31 locators corrected; item 208 missing → planned, item 186 planned → missing; the extraction's own repair of the Proposition 5.5 gap (E6; items 173–188 and 63) checked and found sound, with one step added to 181 and the reference sharpened in 184; 33 new items (3 planned, 30 missing); E1–E17 confirmed (E7, E10, E12 amended); 27 new source issues, among them the Theorem 10.4 error, the resulting gap, 'exactly eleven' in the introduction (fourteen), Proposition 1.2 false for schemes with isolated points, gaps in Theorem 2.1, Propositions 9.3(iv), 11.2, 11.3 and 14.1, and a false step in Proposition 12.2 whose conclusion holds. The matrices (14) and (16) were recomputed (determinant −4) and are correct.
